General Dynamics stock weighs record backlog after Q3 surge
sum: General Dynamics reported broad-based third-quarter growth on Friday, October 30, as major submarine awards lifted orders and the defense contractor raised its full-year outlook. The company said revenue rose 12.9 percent year over year to 14.6 billion US dollars, while diluted earnings per share increased 15.7 percent to 4.49 US dollars.

The company also reported a 6.8-to-1 book-to-bill ratio and a backlog of 220.3 billion US dollars at quarter-end. Defense orders totaled 93.8 billion US dollars, led by awards for Virginia- and Columbia-class submarines, while Aerospace added 5 billion US dollars in orders.

General Dynamics said total estimated contract value reached 270.7 billion US dollars, including 50.4 billion US dollars in potential value from unfunded contracts and unexercised options. The figures point to substantial contracted work ahead, although delivery timing and execution remain important for revenue conversion and margins.
The company provided the results in its third-quarter results release.

Amy Johnson became president of General Dynamics Information Technology on Tuesday, November 3. The company announced the appointment on October 23, saying Johnson brought 27 years of experience across engineering, cybersecurity, defense electronics, space and intelligence systems. Her move places a long-serving Mission Systems executive at the helm of the technology unit.
General Dynamics stock traded at 317.75 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:56 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of General Dynamics stock.
In the broader market, the S&P 500 remains the relevant benchmark for this US-listed defense and aerospace company.

General Dynamics stock slips as record backlog meets raised outlook
sum: General Dynamics reported broad-based third-quarter growth on October 30, led by Marine Systems and strong defense bookings. The company raised its full-year 2026 earnings outlook after revenue climbed 12.9% year over year to $14.6 billion, according to the General Dynamics results release.

Orders totaled $98.8 billion in the quarter, including $93.8 billion in the defense businesses. The resulting backlog reached $220.3 billion, while estimated potential contract value added another $50.4 billion.

Marine Systems was the main growth engine. Quarterly revenue increased 21.1% to $5.0 billion, and operating earnings rose 34.4% to $391 million. The company linked the expansion to higher construction volumes for Columbia-class and Virginia-class submarines, among other programs.

General Dynamics now expects 2026 diluted earnings per share of $17.20 to $17.30, compared with its prior range of $16.80 to $16.90. The forecast also calls for revenue of $56.5 billion to $56.8 billion and an operating margin near 10.5%.

The company generated $1.7 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter and reduced total debt by $500 million. At the same time, capital expenditure reached $481 million, with management expecting full-year capital spending of 3.5% to 4% of sales.

General Dynamics stock traded at 317.55 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:43 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026, 2.02 percent below the Xetra close of Thursday, November 5. The quote was also 2.73 percent below the 326.45-euro level in the November 4 report on the company, a separate comparison from the Xetra day move. The real-time quote of General Dynamics stock provides the latest trading view.

US Defense Stocks Plunge as Democrats Poised for Midterm Landslide; Doubts Mount Over $1.5 Trillion Defense Budget
sum: Defense stocks fell across the board on the US stock market on Nov. 4. Following projections that Democrats will capture both the House and Senate in the midterm elections, concerns spread that Congress will tighten its grip on Pentagon spending plans and new procurement programs.

The steepest decliner was Lockheed Martin (LMT), down 6.9%. RTX (RTX), which makes missiles and radar systems, fell about 3%, and L3Harris Technologies (LHX) dropped more than 6%. General Dynamics (GD) and Northrop Grumman (NOC) also were sold off. The S&P 500 aerospace and defense sub-index is down about 1% year to date, and the Dow Jones US aerospace and defense sub-index is down 3.4%, with the day's losses pushing their year-to-date performance into negative territory.

The defense sector had until now been buoyed by President Trump's proposed $1.5 trillion (approximately ¥236.9 trillion) military budget for fiscal 2027 — a large-scale increase — and by rising demand for missiles and air defense systems tied to the Iran war. However, the prevailing view is that the Democratic-led House will impose stricter scrutiny on the defense budget and new programs.

Jefferies analysts wrote in a report that they expect the fiscal 2027 defense budget to settle at a level closer to the roughly $1.15 trillion (approximately ¥181.6 trillion) proposed by the House, rather than the $1.5 trillion sought by the administration. Roman Schweizer, an analyst at TD Cowen, said "Trump's 'signature' programs are dead," indicating that the nationwide missile defense initiative "Golden Dome" and the "Golden Fleet" modernization plan centered on new "Trump-class" battleships will take a hit.

On the other hand, according to Schweizer, programs related to nuclear force modernization — such as the B21 bomber manufactured by Northrop and the new intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) "Sentinel" — carry the lowest risk. Analysts broadly share the view that support for military modernization itself will largely be maintained, which is keeping full-blown pessimism in check.
Note: Declines are intraday figures. GD and NOC are listed as "under selling pressure" because specific decline percentages were not disclosed.

items.t: U.S. stocks surge, and the Dow soars 1,500 points as oil prices tumble following the U.S. midterm elections
sum: NEW YORK — U.S. stocks soared Wednesday after U.S. President Donald Trump’s party lost its sole control of Washington in the midterm elections.

Stocks generally do well in the months following any midterm U.S. election, regardless of who wins, and the S&P 500 jumped 1.6 per cent for its best day in three months. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied 1,569 points, or 3 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 1.4 per cent.

Stocks of hospital owners and dollar stores serving low-income Americans helped lead the widespread rally following the nationwide losses for Republicans. Investors, meanwhile, see risks ahead for Trump’s social-media company, the artificial-intelligence industry and businesses owned by Elon Musk, who donated heavily to Republicans.

The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil also tumbled below US$95 and touched its lowest level in two months. Vice President JD Vance blamed Republicans’ midterm losses on the war with Iran, which caused a spike in oil prices.

Strategists along Wall Street had been urging investors not to get swept up in the election because it may not matter much for the broad market in the long term. Prices for stocks depend more on where profits for companies and interest rates are heading than on who controls what in Washington.
“Earnings trump elections,” according to Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management.

Still, Wall Street may have gotten a preferred political scenario as Democrats are set to take control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Wall Street generally prefers split control of Washington because it lessens the risk of transformative changes to the economy.

General Dynamics (GD) Q3 Earnings Lift Guidance As Backlog Hits Record
sum: General Dynamics stock barely budged after its Q3 2026 report, ticking up about 0.5% to US$372.59. For a defense contractor posting double digit year on year revenue of US$14.57b and net earnings of US$1.23b, that is a muted response. Traders focused on the day's small move. Long term holders are more likely watching something else entirely.

The real story sits in the order book and cash engine. Management reported record backlog at roughly US$220b and raised full year earnings guidance to a range of US$17.20 to US$17.30 per share. That kind of contracted visibility, paired with strong free cash flow, matters far more than a one day pop.

sum: - General Dynamics reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$14,566 million and net income of US$1,229 million, with earnings per share from continuing operations above the prior year on both a basic and diluted basis and growth across all four segments.
- The business recorded US$98.8b in quarterly orders and a US$220.3b backlog, highlighting a large pipeline of contracted work that has not yet flowed through to reported revenue or earnings.
- This article considers how General Dynamics' investment narrative relates to this record backlog and the stronger than expected third quarter earnings.
Scan beyond General Dynamics and compare this record defense demand with other contractors competing for long-term government budgets using our 30 resilient stocks with low risk scores.

To own General Dynamics, you need to be comfortable with a long pipeline of contracted work turning into cash over time rather than rapid swings in short term revenue. The record US$220.3b backlog, US$270.7b in total estimated contract value and broad based Q3 segment growth all speak to that execution story. The most important near term catalyst is how efficiently those large submarine, aerospace and technology programs move from order book into higher margin production.

The biggest current risk sits in execution and complexity. Issues like the Mesquite munitions plant show how production ramps can create cost overruns, delays and pressure on segment profitability if not fixed quickly. The latest quarter does not remove that risk, although the 20 basis point operating margin expansion and strong cash generation suggest management is currently handling scale reasonably well.

The most relevant recent announcement for this backdrop is the Q3 2026 report itself. General Dynamics reported US$14,566 million in quarterly sales and US$1,229 million in net income, with basic EPS from continuing operations of US$4.55 and diluted EPS of US$4.49. Sales and earnings for the first nine months of 2026 were also above the prior year, supported by demand across all four segments.

sum: General Dynamics enters the final trading session before its scheduled third-quarter report with a marked change from the company-specific stock update examined in our October 28 report. At 16:30:06 Berlin time on October 29, Lang & Schwarz quoted the shares at 330.25 euros. That was 5.04 percent above the Xetra close of October 28 at 314.40 euros.

The upcoming reporting date is the immediate focus. General Dynamics' investor-relations page lists the release of its 2026 third-quarter financial results and conference call, while a Yahoo Finance preview published October 29 says the report is expected before the bell on October 30. The preview cites a market expectation for year-on-year revenue growth of 6.6 percent.

The latest comparable own report recorded a Lang & Schwarz quote of 318.35 euros at 07:53 Berlin time on October 28. The new quote is 11.90 euros higher, equivalent to a 3.74 percent increase. This comparison is separate from the Xetra daily move and reflects different dates and trading conditions.

The operating baseline remains the second quarter. General Dynamics reported revenue of 14.094 billion US dollars and diluted earnings per share of 4.24 US dollars for the period ended July 5, 2026. The Yahoo Finance preview notes that the company had beaten revenue expectations in that quarter. Investors now have to assess whether demand, margins and the full-year outlook remain on track in the new report.

General Dynamics' portfolio spans business jets, naval shipbuilding, combat vehicles and technology services. The company identifies Aerospace, Marine Systems, Combat Systems and Technologies as its four operating divisions. The stock trades primarily on the NYSE under ticker GD.

items.t: General Dynamics (GD) Tops Q2 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
sum: General Dynamics (GD) came out with quarterly earnings of $4.24 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.95 per share. This compares to earnings of $3.74 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +7.34%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this defense contractor would post earnings of $3.68 per share when it actually produced earnings of $4.1, delivering a surprise of +11.41%.
Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

General Dynamics, which belongs to the Zacks Aerospace - Defense industry, posted revenues of $14.09 billion for the quarter ended June 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.48%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $13.04 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.
The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.
General Dynamics shares have added about 16.8% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 8.5%.
While General Dynamics has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?
